# 04 -- GNSS coordinate systems and signal gaps (research brief)

Status: brief, 2026-11-20, seed for the next R&D plan. Asked by the owner after brief 03 (altitude):
(1) China's geodetic datum differs from the US one, so BeiDou and GPS coordinates may disagree;
(2) vehicles in tunnels / underground car parks lose the signal -- how are the missing points inferred and queried?

## 1. Datums: what each system reports

| System | Datum | Ellipsoid | Geocentric | Offset to WGS-84 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPS | WGS-84 | WGS-84 | yes | 0 |
| BeiDou (BDS) | BDCS, realises CGCS2000 | CGCS2000 | yes | **centimetres** (both are aligned to ITRF) |
| China national, since 2008-07-01 | CGCS2000 | CGCS2000 | yes | centimetres |
| Xi'an 1980 (Xi'an geodetic origin, Jingyang) | Xian80 | IAG-75 | **no** | **tens to ~100+ m**, varies by place, needs a 7-parameter transform |
| Beijing 1954 | BJ54 | Krassovsky | no | similar order to Xian80 |
| Map APIs (Amap, Tencent) | GCJ-02 | WGS-84 + deliberate non-linear offset | -- | **~hundreds of m** |
| Baidu | BD-09 | GCJ-02 + second offset | -- | ~hundreds of m |

Correction to the premise: the "Xi'an-centred" datum is **Xi'an 1980**, which was replaced by CGCS2000 as the national
standard in 2008. **Raw BeiDou and raw GPS fixes agree to centimetres; the ellipsoid difference is negligible.**
Large disagreements in practice come from (a) GCJ-02 / BD-09 map offsets, (b) legacy Xian80 / BJ54 survey data,
(c) receiver accuracy (meters, worse in urban canyons). So the audit in brief 03 (G1) is the first step for both briefs.

## 2. Signal gaps (tunnels, underground car parks, urban canyons)

What can be inferred, from cheapest to best:

| Method | Needs | Error in a 2 km tunnel | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linear interpolation by time between the last fix before and the first fix after | the two fixes | small for a straight tunnel, large on curves | do it at query time; no storage |
| Map matching onto the road network (HMM, e.g. OSRM / Valhalla / GraphHopper) | road graph | road-level (tunnel geometry is known) | best value for vehicles; also fixes urban-canyon drift |
| Dead reckoning: speed + heading (+ wheel odometer / IMU) | vehicle CAN / IMU data | grows with time, ~1-3 % of distance | only if the devices report it |
| Car parks: entry fix + exit fix + dwell time | gate/entry geometry | the building, not the slot | floor/slot needs non-GNSS (Bluetooth beacons, gate logs) |

Store inferred points **with a flag and an uncertainty radius** (`src = gnss | interp | matched | dr`, `acc_m`),
never mixed silently with measured ones.

## 3. Query side (Doris)

- Gap detection: `LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle ORDER BY ts)`; a gap = dt > k * report interval.
- "Which vehicles were inside polygon P between t1 and t2" must not miss a vehicle whose fixes straddle P:
  query **trajectory segments** (LINESTRING of consecutive fixes) with `ST_Intersects`, not only points with
  `ST_Contains`. The plan 01 cell index extends to segments by covering each segment (S2 polyline cover).
- Uncertainty-aware answer: inside / maybe-inside (distance to the boundary < `acc_m`) / outside.

## 4. Proposed next plan (outline, English, to be written with org_plan)

- G1: datum audit on real data (shared with brief 03 G1): share of WGS-84 / CGCS2000 / GCJ-02 / BD-09 / Xian80;
  convert to one datum on load.
- G2: gap statistics on real tracks: gaps per vehicle-day, length distribution, share in tunnels / car parks.
- G3: inferred points with `src` + `acc_m`, map matching first (offline batch), interpolation as the fallback.
- G4: segment-based polygon query + the inside / maybe / outside answer, measured against a ground-truth drive.

## 5. What is needed from the owner

- A sample of real tracks (vehicle id, ts, lon, lat, speed, heading, source system) incl. tunnel / car-park trips.
- Which map/provider produced the polygons, and whether the devices are BeiDou-only, GPS-only or multi-GNSS.
